name: browser-frame
purpose: A browser window that renders live webkit components inside a viewport of its own, so a page or story can show a real screen at a real device size — desktop, tablet or mobile — and resize it by hand. The default slot is teleported into an internal `iframe`, which gives the content a true width × height viewport: CSS breakpoints fire against the frame's simulated width, viewport units resolve against its simulated height, and content taller than the viewport scrolls inside it like a page. When the simulated width is wider than the space available, the frame scales the whole viewport down to fit instead of clamping it. The chrome's window dots, address and size readout are decoration; its one control is a copy button inside the address bar, and the frame's other controls are the resize handles on its right edge, bottom edge and bottom-right corner.
useWhen: Showing a real screen — a site band, a console page, a template — built from webkit components, at a device size you choose.
Letting a reader drag a layout from desktop to tablet to mobile to see how it responds, on a documentation page.
Pinning a composed example to a device size (`v-model:width` + `v-model:height`) so a story or page always shows the tablet or mobile layout.
Showing that a result lives at a URL — a deployed site, a preview link — by setting `address`.
avoidWhen: For a static screenshot or clip in documentation → use `doc-frame`.
For third-party content loaded from another origin → use `embed`.
For a mock of the Azion console's own shell on a marketing band → use the console shell mockup the page composes; it draws the console chrome and staggers its parts.

For content whose layout depends on an overlay (`dialog`, `drawer`, a dropdown panel) or a JS breakpoint composable — those still read the outer page (see States), so the frame cannot show them at the simulated size.
For a framed page section or grid cell → use `frame-box`.
related: doc-frame` — the documentation figure frame for stills and clips; no live viewport.
embed` — a titled `iframe` for another origin's document; `browser-frame` renders our own components.
frame-box` — the page's registration frame (hairlines + corner marks), not a window.
copy-button` — the clipboard control the address bar composes; reach for it directly to copy any other value.
bestPractices: Compose the default slot exactly as the screen would be composed in an app — the frame mirrors the page's stylesheets and theme into its viewport, so no extra wiring or classes are needed.
Pin the device the example is about with `v-model:width` and `v-model:height` (`375 × 812` mobile, `768 × 1024` tablet, `1280 × 800` desktop); leave `width` unset to fill the container.
Give the frame an `ariaLabel` that names what is shown (`Pricing page at tablet size`); it becomes the viewport's accessible name.
Viewport-height units (`h-screen`, `min-h-dvh`) in slot content resolve against the simulated height, so a full-height shell renders as it would on the device.
Do not add controls to the chrome — the address's copy button and the resize handles are the frame's only controls. Interactive content belongs in the default slot.

props.name: address
props.doc: Read-only URL shown in the chrome's address bar; the address bar is not rendered when empty.

props.name: minWidth
props.doc: Smallest viewport width the resize handles can reach, in pixels.

props.name: maxWidth
props.doc: Largest viewport width the resize handles can reach, in pixels; widths wider than the container are scaled down to fit.

props.name: minHeight
props.doc: Smallest viewport height the resize handles can reach, in pixels.

props.name: maxHeight
props.doc: Largest viewport height the resize handles can reach, in pixels.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the viewport; when empty it falls back to `address`, then to `Preview`.

props.name: copyAriaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the address bar's copy button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Copy address`).

props.name: widthHandleAriaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the right-edge width handle. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Resize preview width`).

props.name: heightHandleAriaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the bottom-edge height handle. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Resize preview height`).

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The live content, teleported into the frame's viewport `iframe` once it is ready. Renders client-side only.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import BrowserFrame from '@aziontech/webkit/browser-frame'
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import CallToAction from '@aziontech/webkit/call-to-action'
  import CardGrid from '@aziontech/webkit/card-grid'
  import FrameBox from '@aziontech/webkit/frame-box'
  import SectionContainer from '@aziontech/webkit/section-container'
  import SectionGap from '@aziontech/webkit/section-gap'
  import SectionModule from '@aziontech/webkit/section-module'
  import SectionTitle from '@aziontech/webkit/section-title'
  import Topic from '@aziontech/webkit/topic'
</script>

<template>
  <BrowserFrame
    address="https://www.azion.com"
    aria-label="Azion platform page"
  >
    <SectionContainer max-width="site">
      <SectionGap
        size="small"
        hatch
      />
      <SectionModule
        :divided="false"
        :padded="false"
      >
        <template #header>
          <SectionTitle
            kind="horizontal"
            eyebrow="Platform"
            title="Build, secure and deliver from one platform"
            description="Run your applications, protect them and cache their responses on the same distributed network."
          >
            <template #actions>
              <Button
                kind="outlined"
                label="See all products"
              />
            </template>
          </SectionTitle>
        </template>
        <FrameBox
          flush
          borders="y"
          marks="all"
        >
          <CardGrid
            flush
            kind="frame"
            :columns="3"
            :mobile-columns="1"
          >
            <CardGrid.Cell kind="canvas">
              <Topic
                :heading-level="3"
                icon="ai ai-edge-application"
                title="Applications"
                description="Deploy web apps and APIs close to every user, with no servers to provision."
              />
            </CardGrid.Cell>
            <CardGrid.Cell kind="canvas">
              <Topic
                :heading-level="3"
                icon="ai ai-edge-firewall"
                title="Firewall"
                description="Stop DDoS, bots and injection attacks before a request reaches your origin."
              />
            </CardGrid.Cell>
            <CardGrid.Cell kind="canvas">
              <Topic
                :heading-level="3"
                icon="ai ai-tiered-cache"
                title="Tiered Cache"
                description="Answer repeat requests from the nearest location and offload your origin."
              />
            </CardGrid.Cell>
          </CardGrid>
        </FrameBox>
      </SectionModule>
      <SectionGap
        size="small"
        hatch
      />
      <SectionModule
        :divided="false"
        :padded="false"
      >
        <CallToAction
          framed
          kind="split"
          eyebrow="Get started"
          title="Deploy your first application."
          title-muted="Run it everywhere."
          description="Start on the free plan and move to production when you are ready. No credit card required."
        >
          <template #actions>
            <Button
              kind="secondary"
              label="Start for free"
            />
          </template>
          <template #aside>
            <Button
              kind="outlined"
              label="Talk to a specialist"
            />
          </template>
        </CallToAction>
      </SectionModule>
      <SectionGap
        size="small"
        hatch
      />
    </SectionContainer>
  </BrowserFrame>
</template>
